title: Substrate: enforce outcome-based work partitioning before agent execution
description: US-025 required eleven hours, 57 changed files, and 47 commits because an oversized functional story entered execution together with mutation-tool hardening; its initial feature phase alone lasted 3 hours 13 minutes and repeated source changes invalidated cold campaigns. Its final unchanged warm mutation campaign was 72.8598x faster (72.86x rounded), proving cache performance was not the sizing failure: the remaining 26-minute cold path is an optimization target, while admission of oversized mixed scope is the planning defect. Before any US or CHG becomes execution-ready, Substrate should require machine-readable work ID/kind/work type/source, one independently demonstrable outcome, complete parent acceptance-criterion mapping, scopes and boundary signals, phase estimates, uncertainties with resolution or explicit impact, dependencies, decision, partitions, digest-bound approval provenance, checkpoints, and estimate-versus-actual fields. It should centrally enforce every normal hard limit: at most 120 estimated minutes, one primary outcome, three major scopes, two routes/screens, three acceptance flows, 20 expected files, one lifecycle/concurrency boundary, no combined functional delivery and tooling/framework change, no unbudgeted unresolved uncertainty, and no unofficial or unresolved work-item ID. Oversized parents must remain non-executable while Substrate proposes vertical children, allocates official child IDs, preserves complete parent AC mapping and acyclic dependencies, emits a separate approved readiness artifact per child, and records an explicit, reasoned, auditable human override only when genuinely required. Functional and technical changes use the same gate: partition functional work by vertical user/business outcomes and technical work by independently verifiable operational outcomes; mixed work is never an exemption. Generated packages should carry canonical payload digests and approval evidence and enforce the same decision through every agent entry point, the commit hook, staged and Git-range validation, and the repository gate, while generated CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md guidance keeps the rule durable. At 45 minutes require on-track/variance evidence; at 90 minutes stop incomplete implementation and return it for official partitioning. Calibration must retain actual phase minutes, total, changed files, commits, review-fix loops, authoritative cold attempts, source-change invalidations, estimate variance, and root cause, then use historical project evidence to recommend better outcome boundaries, phase budgets, and further safe cold-shard/graph optimization. CHG-022 intentionally excludes generated mirrors CODEX.md, .cursorrules, and .github/copilot-instructions.md because its immutable approval lacks those paths; extending them requires a separate approved digest-bound change, not silent scope growth.

## Authority clarification — supersedes AC4 blocker interpretation above

After reading the approved US-070 design, AC4 is **source-supported under the approved selection-plus-held-commit policy**, with a concrete temporal residual, not a proven binding-contract violation. The design at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-05-us-070-daily-person-activity-design.md:123-127 says: “Select active accounts with `ingestion_mode=api`” and “Manual/CSV accounts are excluded before credential reads and provider calls”. At129-133 it explicitly requires: “Revalidate ingestion mode before committing an API batch so disabling an account during a fetch prevents a stale write” and acknowledges calls already in flight cannot be undone. At139-140 “Mode-excluded accounts” make no calls. The specified selection occurs before calls and is implemented; the design does not say refresh selection before starting each later account, nor define each-account start as a new authorization boundary. Treating every configuration change after global selection as requiring zero subsequent calls would silently strengthen this temporal policy.

The later-B counterexample remains source-conclusive as behavior: A/B initially selected API, B set manual before its first call while A runs, B fetched once then discarded. It is not a fresh execution result. It demonstrates a long cached-selection interval, distinct from an unavoidable toggle after a fresh query. Existing oracles cover exclusion at selection and revocation during fetch; no assertion defines later-account start freshness. Hence this reviewer retracts any unconditional parent blocker and recommends recording the exact residual in the approval package. A stricter per-account-start requirement needs an explicit authority disposition rather than inference from the general zero-call phrase.

US-071 repaired the observed activity-null stop before beginning cost and rechecks each cost day; its accepted survivors36/40/84 concern restart/activation after re-enable, preserving current cost queries. These do not affirm or reject the activity cached-selection interval. They establish the delivered cost temporal policy, not a new stronger activity policy. A new activity prefetch query would reduce the interval but cannot promise absolute zero calls across a concurrent toggle; holding configuration locks throughout provider I/O would be a substantially different design.

If the human chooses stronger per-account-start semantics, a bounded repair estimate is35–60 active minutes plus justified gate time: add active API/support prefetch query before credential reads for each account in apps/worker/src/jobs/analytics-activity.ts; add one real-DB/Pact-backed deterministic later-B disable-before-first-call oracle in analytics-activity.integration.test.ts (assert no B transport/credential observation and no B records; preserve independent channels). No implementation or test is authorized by this review itself.
